in_text_mentions: The MRI of the right hip showed a well-defined intraosseous lesion at the right proximal metadiaphyseal region of the femur involving the neck, greater trochanter, and proximal shaft. The lesion demonstrated hyperintensities on T2 and hypointensities on T1, with a fluid-fluid level. There was a pathological fracture in the intertrochanteric region involving this lesion. The findings on the MRI were consistent with the diagnosis of a unicameral bone cyst, revealing a benign bone lesion at the proximal meta-diaphysis of the right femur with a pathological fracture (Figure 2).

in_text_mentions: A plain radiograph of the right humerus (Figure 1) shows centrally located, well-defined radiolucent lesions with a narrow transition zone and a thin sclerotic margin in the proximal humerus extending to the mid-shaft. There is no periosteal reaction or soft tissue shadow seen; however, there is an expansion of the bone with thinning of the cortex without any breach of the cortex or fracture. It also appears to be in varus deformity in the mid-humerus region.

in_text_mentions: ; Discovery CT 750HD; GE Healthcare, Waukesha, WI, USA) confirmed a pathologic DRF AO type 23-C2 as a result of a bone cyst. The lesion was surrounded by a sclerotic rim measured 3.8 × 2.3 × 1.7 cm (length × width × height) and displayed a cyst index of 3.77 [3]. The intra-cavity density ranged between 40–55 Hounsfield Units (resembling blood). The radiographic findings are summarized in Figure 1. Taken together, the lesion was highly suggestive of a unicameral bone cyst (UBC). Differential diagnoses included an aneurysmatic bone cyst (ABC), a giant cell tumor (GCT) or a non-ossifying fibroma.

findings.label: Expansile cystic lesion
findings.evidence: intramedullary expansile lytic lesion in the proximal metadiaphysis of the humerus

panels.rationale: Single-panel coronal MRI of the left shoulder/upper humerus in a real patient. The caption and in-text report an intramedullary expansile lytic lesion in the proximal metadiaphysis with a focal cortical break and periosteal reaction, consistent with a simple/unicameral bone cyst with pathologic fracture. Findings map directly to the unicameral bone cyst vocabulary; disease attribution is supported by the caption-specific manifestation and the disease-focused article title. No age or ethnicity stated in caption/in-text.
panels.attribution_text: Sahu et al. An Atypical Presentation of a Unicameral Bone Cyst in the Left Humerus: A Case Report.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.64679. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Coronal MRI showing intramedullary expansile lytic lesion in the proximal metadiaphysis of the humerus MRI: magnetic resonance imaging
in_text_mentions: The doctor recommended a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan of the left humerus for further evaluation. The MRI report revealed an intramedullary expansile lytic lesion in the proximal metadiaphysis of the humerus, with a focal cortical break along the inferior aspect of the lesion and an adjacent periosteal reaction, consistent with an SBC with a pathological fracture. The shoulder joint, surrounding soft tissues, and muscles appeared normal, as illustrated in Figure 2.

panels.rationale: Single-panel left shoulder/humerus radiograph of a real patient showing a well-defined expansile multiloculated lucent cystic lesion of the proximal humerus at the metaphyseal-diaphyseal junction with cortical thinning and a pathologic fracture. The article title and caption explicitly attribute the lesion to a unicameral (simple) bone cyst, and the in-text description supports it. Typicality set to atypical because the article title explicitly labels the presentation as atypical (and the multiloculated, metaphyseal-diaphyseal appearance is not the textbook metaphyseal pattern). No age or ethnicity is stated in the caption or in-text mentions; skin tone not assessable on a radiograph. The 'L' laterality marker is a radiographic marker rather than a figure annotation.
panels.attribution_text: Sahu et al. An Atypical Presentation of a Unicameral Bone Cyst in the Left Humerus: A Case Report.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.64679. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Humerus radiograph showing associated multiloculated expansile bone cyst in the left proximal humerus
in_text_mentions: The doctor advised an X-ray of the shoulder joint and humerus for radiological evaluation. The humerus radiograph revealed a well-defined, expansile, multiloculated cystic lesion in the proximal humerus involving the metaphyseal-diaphyseal junction, with a pathological fracture likely indicative of an SBC. No subluxation or dislocation was observed, as illustrated in Figure 1.

panels.rationale: The image is an axial MRI of the wrist showing a well-defined, homogenous hyper-intense cystic lesion in the lunate, which is the characteristic appearance of a unicameral bone cyst. This corresponds to the target disease and vocabulary, and is explicitly stated to be in an adult.
panels.attribution_text: Gündeş et al. Unicameral bone cyst of the lunate in an adult: case report.. Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research 2010. doi:10.1186/1749-799x-5-79. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Magnetic Resonance (MR) imaging views on fat-suppressed T2 weighted sequences have revealed a homogenous hyper-intense cystic lesion in the lunate with smooth and round contours.
in_text_mentions: n normal limits. AP and lateral radiograph of the wrist revealed a radiolucent lesion measuring 11 mm in diameter at the center of the lunate with round margins (Figure 1). There was no scalloping, septae formation or cortical thinning. Computed Tomography (CT) scans of the wrist revealed a round hypodense cystic lesion of 10 mm in diameter without septae formation (Figure 2). Magnetic Resonance (MR) imaging views on coronal fat-suppressed and axial and sagittal T2 weighted sequences have revealed a homogenous hyper-intense cystic lesion in the lunate with smooth and round contours (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Histological section (Elastica van Gieson's stain) of a unicameral bone cyst showing scattered giant cells, consistent with the caption description. B: Histological section (Elastica van Gieson's stain) of a unicameral bone cyst showing a fibrinous membrane surrounded by blood cells, consistent with the caption description.
panels.attribution_text: Massen et al. Pathologic fracture of the distal radius in a 25-year-old patient with a large unicameral bone cyst.. BMC musculoskeletal disorders 2014. doi:10.1186/1471-2474-15-202. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 5.
panels.figure_caption: Histology. A) The black arrow shows an example of scattered giant cells; B) the black arrow shows a fibrinous membrane and some blood cells (elastica van Gieson’s stain).
in_text_mentions: The histopathological workup of the specimen revealed scattered giant cells and remains of fibrous membranes surrounded by red and white blood cells. There were no signs of any malignant transformation. The lesion was classified as a unicameral bone cyst (UBC). Two representative histological sections are presented in Figure 5. The collected material was decalcified with ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) and was stained with picric acid and acid fuchsin (elastica van Gieson’s stain).
